kata.name: Mediator party on a second center - one colleague wired to a legacy hub while every interaction is dispatched by the main hub
kata.series_report: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md mediator row (disposed; discovery-only candidate); fixtures/katas/mediator/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-r5k.5
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: the coherence equations fire on every interaction the second-center colleague participates in; the per-arrow suite is blind because hub_legacy is a declared Mediator row and the documented routes are intact (survived, scoped to second-center topology faults)

expected.detail: bob.hub = hub_legacy while i_ab and i_bc are dispatched by hub_main; the accepted equations dispatched_by = listener;hub (eq0) and dispatched_by = speaker;hub (eq1) emit executed violations on i_ab (bob listens) and i_bc (bob speaks). The per-arrow sample cannot compose the two arrows and misses it

commands: python3 prototype/mediator_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: baseline reports no detection on this fixture
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/mediator/party-second-center.ct.json --json  # exit 3, 2 violations

comparison.conventional_baseline: the frozen per-arrow suite asserts every colleague's hub resolves to a declared mediator, every interaction's parties and dispatch resolve, and every documented route matches; all pass, because a second declared hub is legal data and no assertion composes speaker/listener with hub.

baseline.artifact: prototype/mediator_baseline.py sha256:863b8c04a045b7571242b172540e0ba172aece8df9071ba37dd0263460b456d3 (frozen per-arrow suite: hub/party/dispatch range assertions plus the documented-route table; always executed before the probe arm)

expressibility_gap.invariant: the colleague wired to a foreign hub is reported as the faulting row
expressibility_gap.why: both accepted equations are Interaction-sourced, so the witness row is always an interaction; the colleague appears only through the interactions it participates in, and a colleague with no interactions would be invisible. No Colleague-sourced coherence law exists

discrepancies: The law names the breach (each interaction the second-center colleague joins), not the root cause (the colleague's hub cell); the kernel has no colleague-level witness surface for this fault.
procedure: 1. The law was named before any fixture was written (README: dispatch coherence `dispatched_by = participant ; hub`; exclusivity and absence named as the discovery-only and inexpressible halves). The fault set and its expectations were committed in fixtures/katas/mediator/ (README.md, faults.json) before the recorded run; nothing here is edited after the run.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/mediator_baseline.py, sha256 above) was executed first: per-arrow assertions over every row (colleague hub declared; interaction parties declared and distinct; dispatch declared; documented route matched). It never composes two arrows and never asserts a specific mediator row.
3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real CLI: `catherine check --json`, plus `catherine underconstraint --max-path-length 2 --json` where the discovery question belongs to the entry.

4. Witnesses were mapped to presentation elements (<object>:<name>); unique_detections = executed probe elements minus baseline-identified elements. Hypothesized underconstraint findings are questions, recorded verbatim and never counted as detections.
5. Verdict follows the recorded rule: empty unique = killed; non-empty unique with an executed baseline arm = survived.
